subject: Business
title: Post-Deal Relationship Management
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Post-Deal Relationship Management.

hook.text: A great deal signed on paper means nothing if the relationship collapses during execution.

buildup.text: The real work begins after the handshake. Implementation reveals assumptions both sides got wrong.

discovery.text: Regular check-ins, clear escalation paths, and shared metrics keep both parties aligned after closing.

twist.text: Adversarial negotiators who 'won' often find their partners doing the minimum. Resentment kills execution.

climax.text: Toyota's supplier partnerships last decades because both sides invest in the relationship after every contract.

punchline.text: The best deal is one both sides want to renew.

quiz.question: Why do adversarial negotiation 'wins' often backfire?
options: Resentful partners do the minimum during execution

details.summary: Post-deal relationship management ensures the value negotiated is actually delivered by maintaining communication, resolving issues proactively, and building trust for future interactions.
details.whyItMatters: A deal on paper means nothing until it is implemented. Relationships that deteriorate after signing lead to poor execution, disputes, and missed opportunities for future collaboration.
takeaways: Post-deal relationship management ensures agreed terms are actually delivered
Regular communication prevents small misunderstandings from becoming disputes
Strong post-deal relationships create opportunities for future partnerships

faq.question: What are the most common reasons deals fail after being signed?
faq.answer: Ambiguous terms that both sides interpret differently. Changes in personnel who championed the deal. Shifting business priorities that reduce commitment. Lack of regular communication allowing problems to fester. Failure to adapt terms when circumstances change unexpectedly.

faq.question: How do you maintain a strong relationship after closing a deal?
faq.answer: Schedule regular review meetings. Address issues promptly and directly. Share relevant information proactively. Celebrate milestones together. Be willing to renegotiate terms when circumstances change substantially. Invest in the personal relationship beyond transactional interactions.
